artworks.title: Ulysses at the Court of Alcinous
artworks.description: Hayez's vast Capodimonte canvas shows Odysseus weeping in Alcinous' hall as Demodocus sings of Troy — the Phaeacian king as the perfect host whose court hears the hero's name before the hero will speak it.

artworks.title: Ulysses in the Palace of Alcinous
artworks.description: Lagrenée stages Odyssey 7: the shipwrecked stranger clasps the knees of Alcinous and Arete — Nausicaa's counsel made into a palace tableau of Phaeacian hospitality.

artworks.title: Odysseus before Alcinous, King of the Phaeacians
artworks.description: Malmström's Nationalmuseum painting seats Odysseus before the Phaeacian throne — Alcinous as the island king who will hear the wanderer's tale and send him home on a self-steering ship.

artworks.title: The Banquet in the House of Alcinous, with Homer
artworks.description: Nenci's academic banquet folds Homer himself into Alcinous' feast — a nineteenth-century allegory of the Odyssey's most civilized court, where song, gift, and safe passage still define the king.

popCulture.title: Alcinous
popCulture.description: The Phaeacian king who hosted Odysseus remains the type of perfect hospitality — ships that know the way, and a court of dance and gift.

films.title: Ulysses
films.description: Jacques Dumesnil's Alcinous hosts the amnesiac stranger who almost weds Nausicaa — Phaeacian hospitality as the frame for Kirk Douglas' voyage.

films.title: The Odyssey
films.description: Jeroen Krabbé's Alcinous rules the court that receives Odysseus after the storm — the island king whose ships know the way home.

films.title: The Odyssey
films.description: Rossi's miniseries keeps the Phaeacian palace — Alcinous hearing Demodocus' song and sending the wanderer home on a self-steering ship.
